kind: source call-chain proof; not binary execution or new runtime failure evidence

facts: MoveBlock initializes [BP.MEReturn] to0, validates/locks handles and length before XMSSVC XMS_MOVEBLOCK.
After XMSSVC it directly calls LDSblA20; no intervening test of host AX/BL.
MEM2_Exit restores saved BX and sets AX=1 unless [BP.MEReturn] is nonzero; failure uses that stack-local byte.
LDsblA20 is the far pointer to _text:FLclDsblA20.
FLclDsblA20 returns AX=1 directly for fInHMA, otherwise calls LocalDisableA20.
LocalDisableA20 success assigns AX=1 and clears BL. Its A20 failure has its own error result.
The service table invokes a void function and XMSDispatch returns TRUE independently of its result.

conclusion: Replacing mvdm_xms_cancel_current_operation by setAX(0)/setBL(error) is not a valid error propagation path for this original guest caller. Its ordinary A20/exit path can overwrite the host error and report success. Do not change product behavior on the basis of xmsMoveBlock C header comments alone.
disposition: Keep product cancellation outside B. Do not delete or move it merely to improve layering. A future removal must establish a failure carrier observed by the original caller or an existing outer exception owner, while preserving guest binaries and measuring mirror diff before approval.
excluded_shortcuts: No new B last-error/session cancellation registry
No guest patch or guest rebuild
No new callback table hiding the current F cancellation function
limitations: This proves the checked-in original source call shape; it does not claim disassembly of every deployed HIMEM binary.
No production fault reproduced or new runtime acceptance claimed.
